q: Which intercompany breaks are open and who owns them?

r.response: USD 8.5B of intra-group flows went through Q3; 96.3% was agreed by WD+2 and USD 212M was not. Four causes, each with an owner: goods in transit to the US at 30 September (USD 96M), AstraZeneca China booking US-dollar invoices at the local daily rate (USD 58M), 11 Alexion recharge cost centres mapped to retired group cost centres (USD 41M) and royalty true-ups after the GTN accrual moved (USD 17M). Three mapping-layer rules remove USD 195M of it permanently.

q: Which control deficiencies could affect the Provision 29 declaration?

r.response: Of 1,284 key financial and non-financial controls in Provision 29 scope, 92% are tested for the year and 46% are tested automatically from Snowflake data. 37 deficiencies are open; two are significant: 23 users in AstraZeneca China held conflicting SAP posting and approval roles for more than 30 days, and 4% of third-party HCP payments in two International markets were approved after payment. Both remediations are rules that run daily on governed data, so they can be evidenced before the year-end declaration.

q: How is the RSG restructuring flowing into the Reported-to-Core bridge?

r.response: Q3 reported operating profit was USD 4,387M (27%) and Core operating profit USD 5,855M (36%): USD 1,468M of Core adjustments in the quarter, mostly amortisation of intangibles. The Reshaping for Sustainable Growth programme announced on 30 October adds up to USD 2.0B of one-time restructuring through 2029 for USD 1.5B of annualised benefits. In Q3, 28% of restructuring charges were tagged in entity workbooks after the close; with the RSG tag mandatory at source, every charge flows from provision to the bridge by initiative.

q: What does the ML forecast say for Q4 versus the planners?

r.response: SNOWFLAKE.ML.FORECAST, retrained on 33 months of actuals by therapy area, puts Q4 2026 Total Revenue at USD 16.59B (90% interval 16.21–16.95B), against USD 16.39B in the planners' Q3 Forecast and USD 16.29B in the Budget. Oncology carries most of the upside (ML USD 7.93B vs planners 7.75B). Four of six therapy areas backtest within 5% MAPE and can be accepted as the baseline; CVRM (11.4%, Farxiga LoE) and Vaccines (34.8%, seasonal) stay on the planners' numbers.
